consensus_summary: Consensus treats “bow” as dual referents under one Hebrew term: the war-bow as military power, warfare, strength or divine judgment (breaking it = peace, defeat or end of might), and the rainbow as God’s covenant of mercy/faithfulness; the two are frequently linked by the image of an unstrung or reversed divine bow, with other minor senses (deceitful bow, conquest rider) acknowledged.
book_summary: The bow is a kingdom’s covenant together with the power joined by it; to break the bow is to unstring that kingdom and end its might.
consensus_core_identification: Dual: (1) military/warfare power or judgment (break = peace/defeat); (2) rainbow covenant mercy.
book_core_identification: A single joined reality: kingdom covenant + the power it confers.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus keeps weapon-power and rainbow-covenant as contextually distinct (though linkable) referents; the book fuses them into one symbol of covenanted kingdom-power and applies “break the bow” uniformly to the unstringing of any kingdom’s might.
material_contradiction: None; the book affirms both covenant and power aspects without denying either consensus referent.
rationale: The book’s core preserves the two dominant consensus categories (covenant and power) but materially refines them by treating them as necessarily joined in a single kingdom symbol rather than as alternative or merely analogous senses. This is a boundary and precision change (reclassification of the dual cases under one unified identification), not a replacement of the central referents, so the relation is REFINED rather than MATCH, DIVERGENT or NOVEL.
strongest_objection: The book illegitimately conflates two contextually distinct biblical referents (rainbow-covenant vs. weapon-power) that the consensus tradition keeps separate even when it notes their shared vocabulary or possible imagery link.
